entities.name: Emperor Xian of Han
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emperor Xian of Han, born Liu Xie (劉協) in 181 CE, was the 14th and final emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty, reigning from September 28, 189 CE, until his forced abdication on December 11, 220 CE. His three-decade nominal rule marked the terminal decline of a 400-year imperial tradition and the violent fragmentation of China into the Three Kingdoms period, a pivotal era in East Asian history. Though holding the imperial title, Xian was largely a puppet in the hands of powerful warlords, most notably Dong Zhuo and later Cao Cao, whose struggles for dominance utterly dismantled the central authority of the Han state.

His reign commenced amidst the chaos following the death of Emperor Ling and the subsequent massacre of eunuchs and court officials in Luoyang. Initially elevated by Dong Zhuo, who then held the court captive and moved the capital to Chang'an in 190 CE, Emperor Xian spent much of his youth as a pawn. After Dong Zhuo's assassination in 192 CE, the emperor endured years of flight and destitution, often lacking basic necessities, as various regional strongmen vied for control. By 196 CE, he fell under the sway of Cao Cao, who established the new imperial capital at Xuchang and used the emperor's legitimate authority to issue edicts and consolidate his own power across northern China, effectively governing through the imperial facade.
